plain.li: [greetings,warm,their:healers] Your letter was read by the lamp at the door tonight, {WRITER}. We were spared, and so we owe, and the order counts your colony among those it owes.
[greetings,cordial,their:healers] The order thanks you for your letter, {WRITER}. Your colony's name is written beside the lamp, with the others the sickhouse keeps in its thoughts.
[condolences,warm,their:healers] We have written your dead into the last pages of the Book of the Spared, {WRITER}, where the order keeps those it could not save. They are not forgotten here.
[condolences,cordial,their:healers] The order grieves with you, {WRITER}. Keep a lamp lit for them a while; it helps more than people think.
[warning,warm,their:healers] Your warning came to the ward in good time, {WRITER}. We have moved the sick to the inner rooms and doubled the night watch, and the order will not forget it.
[warning,cordial,their:healers] Thank you for the warning, {WRITER}. The guards are on the walls, and the lamp stays lit whatever comes.
[news,warm,their:healers] Fevers travel faster than news, {WRITER}, and the ward hears of both. Here is what came through our door this season.
[invitation,cordial,their:healers] If the sick can spare one of us, one of us will come, {WRITER}. Keep the lamp lit and we will find your gate.
[greetings,warm,their:herders] Your words came to the fire at dusk, {WRITER}, after the count, which is the best time for words. The elders say your colony may eat from our pot.
[condolences,warm,their:herders] The elders counted your dead with ours at dusk, {WRITER}, one by one, so that the grass will know them. A herder never leaves anyone behind on the road.
[condolences,cordial,their:herders] We are sorry for your loss, {WRITER}. The camp will sing for them when it moves on.
[warning,warm,their:herders] Your rider found us before the trouble did, {WRITER}. The herd is in the far valley with every head counted, and the elders will not forget it.
[warning,cordial,their:herders] We heard your warning, {WRITER}. The herd is moving, and the archers ride its edges.
[invitation,cordial,their:herders] When the grass brings us your way, we will stop at your gate, {WRITER}. The grass will tell when.
[greetings,warm,their:traders] Your colony is in the Waystone Book in good ink, {WRITER}, and the waymasters drank to it. Every caravan of ours on your road knows your gate.
[greetings,cool,their:traders] The league has your letter. The book has room for your name in good ink or in red, and which is up to you.
[condolences,warm,their:traders] The league is sorry for your loss, {WRITER}. We carry our dead home on the road, every one, and we would help you carry yours.
[condolences,cordial,their:traders] Hard news, {WRITER}, and the league is sorry for it. The road is lonelier without them.
[warning,warm,their:traders] Your warning reached the waystation ahead of the trouble, {WRITER}. The caravans are holding, every crate is safe, and the league owes you for it.
[warning,cordial,their:traders] Noted and passed down the road, {WRITER}. The wardens are riding out.
[greetings,warm,their:pilgrims] Your name is among the doors that opened, {WRITER}, and the fellowship says it at every shrine. Peace on your house.
[condolences,warm,their:pilgrims] We said your dead's names at the shrine this morning, {WRITER}, and will say them again at the next. Nobody walks the last road alone.
[condolences,cordial,their:pilgrims] The fellowship mourns with you, {WRITER}. A pilgrim will stop to pray at your graves when the road passes them.
[warning,warm,their:pilgrims] Your warning turned our bands off the bad road, {WRITER}, and every one of them will bless your door for it.
[warning,cordial,their:pilgrims] We have your warning, {WRITER}. The bands will take the long way round.
[greetings,warm,their:scholars] Your letter has been read, copied twice and filed, {WRITER}, as Ilse Varro asked of us. Strictly speaking that is the highest honour the society has, and you have it.
[condolences,warm,their:scholars] We have written your dead into the archive, {WRITER}, with everything your letter said of them. Nothing known should be lost, and they will not be.
[condolences,cordial,their:scholars] The society is sorry for your loss, {WRITER}. If you would write down who they were, we will keep it.
[warning,warm,their:scholars] Your warning reached the archive in time, {WRITER}. The oldest books are in the cellar and the proctors are on the roof, and we have noted who warned us.
[warning,cordial,their:scholars] The society has your warning, {WRITER}, and has filed it. The proctors are on watch.
[greetings,warm,their:brokers] Your message is in the manifest, {WRITER}, beside every bargain the enclave has kept. That is where we keep our friends.
[condolences,warm,their:brokers] The exchange stopped for an hour when your message came, {WRITER}, which it does for nobody. The enclave is sorry for your loss.
[condolences,cordial,their:brokers] Your loss is noted, {WRITER}, and regretted.
[warning,warm,their:brokers] Your warning reached the exchange in time to move the cargo, {WRITER}. Noted, and owed.
[warning,cordial,their:brokers] Warning received and logged, {WRITER}. The marshals are on the pad.
[greetings,warm,their:fishers] Your words came down with the current, {WRITER}, and the landing heard them over the stew. Any boat of ours will carry your people across.
[condolences,warm,their:fishers] We set a light on the water for your dead, {WRITER}, and let the river carry it down to the sea. Everything comes down to the river in the end.
[condolences,cordial,their:fishers] The landing is sorry for your loss, {WRITER}. The river takes everyone to the sea in the end, and it is gentle about it.
[warning,warm,their:fishers] Your warning came down the river ahead of the trouble, {WRITER}. The boats are pulled up and the landing is ready, and we owe you a crossing.
[warning,cordial,their:fishers] We have your warning, {WRITER}. The boats will keep to the far bank.
[arrive,their:healers] I followed the lamps from the sickhouse to your gate.
[deliver,their:healers] From the order, and freely given, as everything of ours is.
[leave,their:healers] Keep a lamp lit, and the order will always find you.
[arrive,their:herders] I rode in after the count, and every head was there.
[leave,their:herders] I must be back before dusk, the count waits for nobody.
[arrive,their:traders] Signed for at the waystone, and here in good time.
[deliver,their:traders] Every crate home, and this one's yours.
[arrive,their:pilgrims] The road brought me to your gate, and peace on it.
[deliver,their:pilgrims] Freely given, as the fellowship gives everything.
[arrive,their:scholars] Copied twice, carried once, and here at last.
[deliver,their:scholars] From the archive, and noted in the ledger.
[arrive,their:brokers] Delivered by hand, on time, as agreed.
[collect,their:brokers] Collected in full, and noted in the manifest.
[arrive,their:fishers] Up from the water, and dry for once.
[deliver,their:fishers] Carried across for a friend, as the river folk do.
[arrive,their:healers] Peace on this house, is anyone here unwell?
[wait,their:healers] I'll wait, the ward taught me patience if nothing else.
[stay,their:healers] A roof and a lamp, that's all a hospitaller asks.
[leave,their:healers] Keep the lamp lit, and send for us if a fever comes.
[pass,their:healers] Back to the ward, the beds won't empty themselves.
[arrive,their:herders] Your grass looks good from the road.
[wait,their:herders] The grass will tell, so I'll wait and see.
[stay,their:herders] A guest eats from the same pot, so I won't refuse your supper.
[leave,their:herders] Back to the herd before dusk, they'll want counting.
[pass,their:herders,animals] Easy now, we're only passing through.
[arrive,their:traders] Fair dealing here, I hope, the book says so.
[wait,their:traders] Take your time, though the road won't.
[stay,their:traders] A word given at the waystone stands, so you'll have no trouble from us.
[leave,their:traders] The road won't wait, so neither will I.
[pass,their:traders] Good ink on this gate, keep moving.
[arrive,their:pilgrims] Peace on this house, and on everyone in it.
[wait,their:pilgrims] Every door is a shrine to someone, so I'll wait by yours.
[stay,their:pilgrims] An open door, and I'll bless it in the morning.
[leave,their:pilgrims] Walk on and bless what you pass, so your gate gets a blessing.
[pass,their:pilgrims] There is no last shrine, so on we go.
[arrive,their:scholars] Strictly speaking I'm early, which is a first.
[wait,their:scholars] I'll wait, I brought a book.
[stay,their:scholars] Any corner with a lamp to read by will do.
[leave,their:scholars] I'll write all this down before I forget a word of it.
[pass,their:scholars] Nothing known should be lost, so on to the next archive.
[arrive,their:brokers] Terms first, then talk, if that suits.
[wait,their:brokers] Waiting is billed at no charge, this once.
[stay,their:brokers] Adequate accommodation, noted with thanks.
[leave,their:brokers] Noted, and the account is in good standing.
[pass,their:brokers] Nobody is stranded who has something to sell.
[arrive,their:fishers] Is the water clean here, or should I ask?
[wait,their:fishers] No hurry, the river isn't going anywhere.
[stay,their:fishers] A dry floor, that's a treat for river folk.
[leave,their:fishers] Back to the water, the river's calling.
[pass,their:fishers] Everything comes down to the river in the end, us too.
[chat,them,their:healers] We were spared, and so we owe, that's all the order really is.
[endwarm,them,their:healers] If you're ever sick, send for us, and we'll come at a run.
[faithtalk,them,their:healers] Aldith never asked anyone whose side they were on, and nor do we.
[chat,them,their:herders] Count them at dusk, my grandmother said, and I always have.
[endwarm,them,their:herders] You'd make a fair herder, if you could stand the walking.
[faithtalk,them,their:herders] Tamsa walked forty head through the dry year, and we still walk where she walked.
[chat,them,their:traders] Good ink or red ink, the book only has the two.
[endwarm,them,their:traders] I'll put in a good word at the next waystation, and they'll write it down.
[faithtalk,them,their:traders] Edda Vane took nine wagons through Harrow Ford, and nobody fired.
[chat,them,their:pilgrims] I have a shell for every shrine, and room on the string for more.
[endwarm,them,their:pilgrims] Your name goes with me to the next shrine, I promise you.
[faithtalk,them,their:pilgrims] Old Brannoc prayed at every people's shrine and never asked whose it was.
[chat,them,their:scholars] Ask the question nobody will, that's the first thing they teach us.
[endwarm,them,their:scholars] This is going in my notes, and my notes go in the archive.
[faithtalk,them,their:scholars] Ilse Varro saved eleven books from the fire, and we've argued about the rest ever since.
[chat,them,their:brokers] A bargain struck is kept to the last digit, or it was never a bargain.
[endwarm,them,their:brokers] Noted, and that means more from us than you'd think.
[faithtalk,them,their:brokers] Okoro sold a dead ship one bargain at a time, and we never stopped selling.
[chat,them,their:fishers] Take what the water gives and no more, and it'll keep giving.
[endwarm,them,their:fishers] If you're ever on the water, ask any river boat to carry you across.
[faithtalk,them,their:fishers] Wenna Reed's boats pulled people off the rooftops for three days, and we count from that.
Strictly speaking, that's two questions.
How would we know it was lost if nobody wrote down that it existed?
I'll argue the other side, just to see if yours holds.
Eleven books saved, and we still argue about the twelfth.
Somebody write that down before we forget who said it.
I concede the point, and only that point.
That's a good question, and nobody here can answer it.
Copy it twice and argue about it once, that's the rule.
What we never wrote down, we lose, and that's the whole argument.

cheerful.li: Nobody's winning, and that's the best part of it.

blunt.li: That's wrong, and I can say why.

plain.li: [opt0] A hospitaller of the order sat with my {TALE} last night. Every time I woke there was a cool cloth and someone awake.
[opt0] The order sent someone for the fever. We were spared, and so we owe, they said, and wouldn't take a thing for it.
[opt1] {X_nameDef} saw to me with our own doctor at the elbow, asking questions all night. I think I got better out of politeness.
[opt2] The order sent a hospitaller for my {TALE} and we said we'd manage. We're managing.

warm.li: [opt0] I don't know {X_nameDef}'s people at all, and {X_pronoun} sat up all night with my fever anyway.

gloomy.li: [opt2] Burning up, and we sent the order's nurse back down the road.

plain.li: [opt0] The fellowship's Long Walk came by, and we stood at our graves with them while their eldest said the old words.
[opt1] We walked the pilgrims back to the road, singing what we could of their song, and waved them on.
[opt2] Pilgrims on their walking day, a long file of them. We gave them food for the road and they blessed the gate twice.
[opt3] A long file of pilgrims stopped to pray here today. I watched them from the wall.
[opt0] Every one of the pilgrims had a string of shells, one for each shrine. Our graves are a shrine to someone now, I suppose.

warm.li: [opt0] Strangers praying over our dead as if they were their own. I didn't expect it to move me.

plain.li: [opt0] Argued with a fellow of the learned society half the night about books that burned before I was born. I think I lost, and I'd do it again.
[opt0] The night of the fire, they call it. Everyone gathered round and I had to argue the colony's side.
[opt1] Spent an hour with {X_nameDef} of the society, who asked the question nobody else would and wrote down every answer.
[opt2] A scholar wanted to hold some kind of disputation here tonight. We had work in the morning.
[opt1] The scholar said strictly speaking I'd asked two questions. I had, and both were good ones, apparently.

cheerful.li: [opt0] Nobody won the argument tonight and nobody wanted it to end. Good night.
